summary.text: Amy Paulin is a Democratic member of the New York State Assembly who has represented District 88 since 2001 and is running for re-election on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines.
She chairs the Assembly Committee on Health.

paragraphs.text: Amy Paulin was born and raised in Brooklyn and graduated from the State University of New York at Albany, where she also earned a master's degree and completed doctoral coursework in criminal justice.
She and her husband, Ira Schuman, have lived in Scarsdale for more than 40 years and raised three children there.

Before her election, Paulin was executive director of My Sisters' Place, served on the Scarsdale Village Board of Trustees, founded and chaired the Westchester Women's Agenda, and was president of the Westchester League of Women Voters and vice president of the New York State League of Women Voters.
Paulin has served the 88th Assembly District since 2001; it includes Scarsdale, Edgemont, Eastchester, Bronxville, Tuckahoe, Pelham, Pelham Manor and parts of New Rochelle and White Plains.

She chaired the Assembly Committee on Energy from 2013 to 2017 and the Committee on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions from 2018 to 2022, and she now chairs the Health Committee and serves on the Rules and Education committees.

Her official biography lists among her legislative work a bill that eliminated the statute of limitations for rape, the Trafficking Victims Protection and Justice Act, and the Birth Control Access Act.
